text_blocks.snippet: Yes, smoking can worsen infections. It weakens the immune system, making it harder to fight off infections, and can also damage the respiratory system, increasing susceptibility to respiratory infections like pneumonia, tuberculosis, and influenza. Furthermore, smoking can negatively impact wound healing, potentially leading to increased risk of wound infections after surgery.

list.title: Weakened Immune System:
list.snippet: Smoking impairs the function of immune cells like neutrophils, making it harder for the body to defend against pathogens.

list.title: Respiratory System Damage:
list.snippet: Smoking damages the delicate tissues of the respiratory tract, making them more vulnerable to infection. It can also reduce the effectiveness of mucus and cilia, which help clear out pathogens.

list.title: Increased Risk of Infections:
list.snippet: Studies show that smokers have a higher risk of various infections, including:
Respiratory Infections: Pneumonia, influenza, tuberculosis, and other respiratory illnesses are more common and severe in smokers.
Wound Infections: Smoking impairs wound healing and increases the risk of infections after surgery or injury.
Other Infections: Smoking can also increase susceptibility to other infections like bacterial vaginosis, sexually transmitted diseases, and certain viral infections.

list.title: Worsened Outcomes:
list.snippet: For those already infected, smoking can worsen the severity and duration of the illness. For example, smoking can make influenza and COVID-19 infections more severe.

list.title: Reduced Immune Response:
list.snippet: Smoking can reduce the effectiveness of the body's immune response, making it harder to clear infections. For example, it can reduce the production of interferons, which are crucial for fighting viral infections.
